extracted.intended_audience: scientists, astronomers, and medical/public-health professionals (readers of Nature)
extracted.subtask_short: scientific observational methods and public-health guidance
extracted.subtask_description: A mixed set of procedural and evaluative recommendations and standards for observational astronomy (astrographic catalogues, comet/meteor observation, spectroheliography) and for medical/public-health practice (physical culture in schools, diagnostic and sanitary precautions). Extracts standards and methodological guidance embedded in scientific news and society reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Astrographic catalogue observation standard
rubrics_metrics.description: With reference to the 10,000 standard stars which have to be observed by means of the transit circle, obtain good positions of all these stars (three observations of each) in ten or twelve years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose to make this list of stars the standard work at the Perth Observatory, observing and re-observing exactly the same list in order to obtain good determinations of the position of each star every ten years or so. Certain zones have already been completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of linear markings on planetary discs (Mars canals)
rubrics_metrics.description: When interpreting so-called canals of Mars, account for optical effects (aberration, diffraction, atmospheric softening) that materially increase the apparent breadth of any linear marking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prof. Newcomb's estimate: a perfectly black line three miles in breadth might be visible on Mars only if surface uniform, but in practice the actual breadth would need to be increased to eight or ten miles to be differentiated; aberration etc. would spread a marking some twenty miles on each side so that the apparent breadth in the telescope could be fifty miles or upward. The large relative area implied by mapped canals requires caution in interpretation; experimental studies of observer interpretation are recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectroheliograph slit selection for sun-spot imaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Set the primary slit on some of the dark lines which are found strengthened in the sun-spot spectrum to emphasise umbra and penumbra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographs taken with the slit on lines strengthened in the umbra and penumbra show these regions much darker and the diameter of the spot considerably increased compared with plates taken with the light of the continuous spectrum. Lines weakened in sun-spots give definite but less marked results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectroheliograph dispersion requirement for faint lines
rubrics_metrics.description: For work with the numerous faint lines of the spot spectrum, a large dispersion is absolutely essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A suitable high-dispersion instrument is required (one is being constructed for use with the new vertical telescope) to resolve and photograph the faint spot-spectrum lines effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of stereoscopic spectroheliograms to detect solar changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain spectroheliograms for stereoscopic examination (pairs taken at short intervals) to reveal masses of flocculi standing above the hemisphere and to detect changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pairs taken at intervals (example given: 2h. 5m.) can be examined in a stereocomparator to detect changes in appearance of flocculi that might otherwise escape detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perseid meteor shower observation protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch the Perseid shower during its apparition and ascertain the hourly number of Perseids visible throughout the nights of August 11 and 12 (probable time of maximum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give special regard to evidence of roughly ten-year periodic enhancements (e.g., 1877, 1887, 1897) and to measure the diurnal motion of the radiant (noted as about one degree toward ENE). Systematic hourly counts across the nights are recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical exercise and school facilities standard for national health
rubrics_metrics.description: Every organ, muscle, and structure in the body requires a proper amount of work to keep it healthy; physical culture is a pressing question for national health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schools should have proper playgrounds and gymnasiums, and trainers in physical exercises are as necessary as school teachers; the medical man should be consulted on the kind of exercise to be employed (i.e., professional medical guidance in organising physical culture).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public guidance on food quantity and nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the public ('the man in the street') should be able to obtain from his medical attendant precise details of the quantity of food required and of its nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medical practitioners should provide clear, precise dietary guidance to the public as part of preventive and personal health measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precautions against dissemination of infectious expectoration
rubrics_metrics.description: Insist on precautions with regard to disinfection and preventing consumptives from disseminating their infectious expectoration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Question whether consumptives should be allowed to stay in hotels and lodgings without taking precautions; emphasises need for practical disinfection measures to control infective diseases (tuberculosis highlighted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of thought and terminology in medicine
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid vague, catch-all medical terms (e.g., 'irregular', 'suppressed gout', 'liver out of order') which cloak ignorance; prefer precise description or confess uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unreflecting adhesion to authority retards correct knowledge; clinicians should use accurate terms and reasoning rather than ambiguous labels, and question asserted selective actions without evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination of public medical services
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary effort (hospitals) and State-aided treatment under the Poor Law have failed to produce adequate results; there is need for coordination of the public medical services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A coordinated system of State-paid and State-directed medical service would be economically justified and should be allied with preventive medicine to improve efficiency and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ophthalmo-reaction with tuberculin as early tuberculosis diagnostic
rubrics_metrics.description: Application to the eye of a 1 per cent solution of dry tuberculin (precipitated by alcohol) produces no reaction in healthy subjects but a characteristic conjunctival redness within twenty-four hours in tuberculous subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reaction has been utilised in nearly a thousand cases with very satisfactory results and has revealed tuberculous lesions in many instances (especially in children) where they had not been suspected; the description gives concentration and expected timeframe for the diagnostic reaction.
